findings.description: Direct inspection of all five V194 views and six pose renders: the neutral skirt still has dense, irregular vertical folds and a puckered waist junction. The crouch shows skirt panels flaring into sharp folded tails with exposed anterior thighs; sit leaves most of the lap area uncovered. Pose-matched ray coverage is only 52/532 triangles (9.8%) in crouch and 22/532 (4.1%) in sit; visual fit remains unacceptable.

V194 front, side, three-quarter, back and prone views still show angular planar folds across the bodice, a gray waist-side patch with unverified garment-surface ownership, and an uneven waist/back transition. The jacket surface remains visibly unfinished.

The V194 per-authored-row line search preserves 108 lap-hem vertices and 262 shared panel-boundary vertices, but minimum orientation-safe row scales remain 0.0141/0.0171 on the two lap panels. Mean applied displacement blend is 0.158; maximum rest displacement is 0.0101 m and maximum nearest-surface distance remains 0.1447 m. Crouch coverage only changes from 48/532 in V193 to 52/532; sit remains 22/532. This is diagnostic prototype geometry, not fit acceptance.

nextAction: Stop tuning row scale, row width, or iteration count. The direct V194 review and pose-ray diagnostics show that even row-local displacement is blocked by low inversion-safe motion on both lap panels (minimum row scales 0.0141/0.0171) while crouch/sit coverage remains 9.8%/4.1%. In Blender, inspect the actual evaluated neutral/crouch/sit cloth mesh and panel connectivity to find where the authored lap topology folds or separates from the front thigh. Change the sewn panel geometry or cloth construction so the lap can move without forcing local triangle inversion; keep the current appearance and fit gates rejected until new renders visibly resolve the skirt, bodice facets, and waist patch.
